State Bank of India Valuation Shifts to Very Expensive Amid Strong Market Returns
sum: On 9 November 2026, SBI’s Mojo Grade was upgraded from Sell to Hold, reflecting a more balanced outlook on the stock’s prospects. The current Mojo Score stands at 54.0, signalling a moderate investment appeal within the public sector banking space. However, the valuation grade has simultaneously shifted from expensive to very expensive, underscoring a growing premium in the stock’s price relative to its earnings and book value.

Specifically, SBI’s P/E ratio is currently at 11.58, which, while appearing modest in absolute terms, is elevated relative to its historical averages and peer group benchmarks. The price-to-book value ratio has risen to 1.75, indicating that the market is pricing SBI at nearly twice its net asset value. This contrasts sharply with other public sector banks, many of which trade at significantly lower multiples.

When benchmarked against its peers, SBI’s valuation premium becomes more apparent. Punjab National Bank (PNB), for instance, trades at a P/E of 7.53 and is rated as attractive, while Union Bank of India and Bank of Baroda are classified as very attractive with P/E ratios of 7.19 and 7.17 respectively. Indian Bank and Canara Bank also maintain lower P/E multiples of 9.56 and 5.93, with fair to very attractive valuations.

The PEG ratio, which adjusts the P/E for earnings growth, further highlights SBI’s stretched valuation at 1.19 compared to PNB’s 0.23 and Union Bank’s 0.41. This suggests that while SBI’s earnings growth prospects are factored in, the premium remains substantial relative to the growth-adjusted valuations of its peers.

SBI’s fundamentals remain solid, supporting its premium valuation to some extent. The bank reported a return on equity (ROE) of 13.22% and a return on assets (ROA) of 1.01%, both respectable figures within the public sector banking industry. However, the net non-performing assets (NPA) to book value ratio stands at 3.09%, indicating ongoing asset quality challenges that investors should monitor closely.
Dividend yield remains modest at 1.53%, reflecting a cautious approach to shareholder returns amid capital conservation and regulatory requirements.

SBI Penny Stocks 2026: State Bank Group
sum: SBI penny stocks refer to two distinct categories of low-price stocks connected to the State Bank of India. The first category includes stocks of companies in which SBI holds a significant stake — the most prominent being Yes Bank, where SBI is the largest shareholder with 23.99% ownership. The second category includes stocks of SBI's own subsidiaries and associates that trade at low price points. Some investors also use the term loosely to mean "PSU bank penny stocks" — public sector bank shares trading below Rs.100.

SBI itself — trading around Rs.750-900 — is not a penny stock by any definition. But its group companies and stake holdings create several proxy entry points for investors who want exposure to the SBI ecosystem at low price points. This article clarifies exactly which stocks qualify, their current fundamental profile, and the risks involved.
SBI penny stocks — Yes Bank, SBFC Finance, SBI-linked companies and PSU bank low-price proxy plays

Yes Bank is the most prominent "SBI penny stock." After Yes Bank's near-collapse in March 2020, a SEBI and RBI-coordinated rescue led by SBI brought a consortium of banks together to infuse Rs.10,000 crore, with SBI taking a 49% initial stake (later reduced). As of 2026, SBI holds 23.99% of Yes Bank — making it the single largest shareholder and an implicit guarantor of the bank's stability.

Yes Bank currently trades in the Rs.18-24 range, placing it firmly in penny stock territory for Indian investors. The bank has undergone significant clean-up of its NPA book, rebuilt its CASA ratio, and diversified its loan book away from large corporates toward retail and MSME lending. The question for penny stock investors is whether Yes Bank's operational recovery translates to significant price appreciation.
Yes Bank data approximate as of early 2026. Verify on BSE/NSE disclosures.

SBFC Finance Limited is a non-banking financial company in which SBI has a meaningful stake. It focuses on small business loans — collateral-backed working capital and machinery finance for MSMEs. Trading in the Rs.80-120 range, SBFC is not a sub-Rs.50 penny stock but qualifies as a low-price small-cap with SBI parentage that many investors classify as part of the SBI group penny stock universe.

Anthropic's $1.5 Trillion IPO Valuation Surpasses India's Top 10 Firms as AI Investment Surges
sum: Anthropic's November 2026 IPO valued the Claude maker at $1.5 trillion, around 32% above the combined $1.14 trillion market capitalisation of India's 10 largest listed companies. Its record $81.3 billion share sale reflects investor appetite for AI, despite rising infrastructure costs and mounting questions about profitability.

Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic has attracted global investor attention after its Nasdaq listing valued the company at approximately $1.5 trillion, exceeding the combined market capitalisation of India's 10 largest listed companies. Founded in 2021, the company behind the Claude chatbot has achieved this valuation in just five years, highlighting the extraordinary pace at which capital is flowing into the global AI industry.

The comparison also raises questions about India's position in the AI investment cycle, particularly when a relatively young technology company commands a higher valuation than the country's largest banking, technology, telecommunications and industrial businesses.
Anthropic's IPO Raises $81.3 Billion at a $1.5 Trillion Valuation

Anthropic priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share on 19 November 2026, exceeding its earlier indicated price range of 70−78. Strong investor demand prompted the company to increase the offering to about 980 million shares, up from the initially planned 825 million.

According to Reuters, the public share offering raised approximately $81.3 billion, making it the largest stock market debut on record. The overall transaction, including a further $26 billion private placement, reached approximately $107.3 billion. This surpassed the previous record associated with SpaceX's public offering.

The valuation stands at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, which includes stock options and restricted shares. On a non-diluted basis, Anthropic's valuation is approximately $1.1 trillion.

The Indian rupee strengthened by 1.66%, or 157 paise, during the week to close at 92.67 per US dollar on 20 November 2026. It traded between 92.64 and 93.74 during the week and crossed the 93-per-dollar level for the first time since 20 April 2026.

FIIs bought equities worth ₹62,158.14 crore during the week and continued their buying streak for the fourth consecutive week. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), however, remained net sellers for the third straight week. They sold shares worth ₹12,698.39 crore. However, their selling pace moderated compared with the previous week. The continued inflows also helped offset selling pressure from domestic institutional investors.

Public sector undertaking (PSU) banks emerged as the strongest-performing sector during the week. The Nifty PSU Bank index rose 6.72%, while the Nifty Bank and Nifty Private Bank indices gained 5.90% and 5.65%, respectively.

FPCE proposes national realty appellate tribunal, statutory exit for homebuyers
sum: Homebuyers’ body FPCE has proposed changes to the RERA Act, including a National Appellate Tribunal for Real Estate, legally binding sale agreements, a statutory exit mechanism and automatic compensation for project delays or deficiencies. The proposals were submitted to Cabinet Secretariat officials on November 12.

An FPCE delegation comprising its president Abhay Upadhyay and members Ratul Mazumder and Jai Pal Raheja presented the suggestions, which also include making real estate regulatory authorities accountable through periodic audits and ensuring automatic compensation to allottees in cases of project delays or deficiencies.

FPCE has proposed establishing a National Appellate Tribunal for Real Estate (NATRE) in Delhi in place of state-level appellate tribunals, with appeals against its decisions lying directly with the Supreme Court.

It said different interpretations of the same central legislation across states have resulted in inconsistent protection for homebuyers. The proposed tribunal would also hear appeals against orders passed by regulatory authorities and adjudicating officers, with virtual benches to avoid requiring homebuyers to travel to Delhi.

The organisation has also sought amendments to Section 13(2) of RERA to place the Agreement for Sale in a schedule to the Act, making it binding. It said the present provision allows state governments to prescribe its format through rules, enabling developers to incorporate clauses that dilute homebuyer protection.

Banks’ data breaches: India in constant state of digital pandemic; new vaccine needed regularly, say experts
sum: Since July, at least seven banks – including the largest lender State Bank of India -- have been victim to data breaches and cybersecurity attacks, causing critical customer data to be exposed to the Dark Web. The regulator, Reserve Bank of India, since October 19, has issued two advisories to lenders to tighten controls and set timelines for controls.

The deeper concern is that when banks give application programming interfaces (APIs) to non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) – by allowing their core systems to exchange data and allow for transactions linked to loan allocations or forex cards, the APIs are the portion which could be most compromised. Attackers – who rarely use the front door to break in – can hijack these trusted connections to carry out fund transfers or customer details from the bank.

In October 2026, while ICICI Bank's internal servers were not breached directly, cybercriminals compromised the APIs which linked ICICI Bank’s systems to NBFCs. Hackers manipulated these payment gateways to trigger over 700 unauthorised instant loan transfers, stealing approximately $2 million (approx. Rs 17 crore), media reports said.
“Historically, NBFCs, fintechs, have always been the weakest link and soft target,” says Yash Kadakia, founder of Security Brigade, a cyber security company.

Despite the heightened sense of caution, experts say banks, besides large corporates, remain in constant risk of future cyber-attacks. “We are in a constant state of digital pandemic. Whenever the new virus is coming, we have to take a vaccination for it,” says Ritesh Bhatia, founder of V4WEB Cybersecurity, who is a cybercrime investigator, incident response expert and data privacy consultant.

Just after announcing the September-ended quarterly earnings, SBI chairman C.S. Setty called the data breach at the bank – announced on October 21 -- in which some customers’ data was exposed on the dark web, “definitely an issue of concern”. SBI had received alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on October 16 that its customers’ data was available on the dark web.

sum: State Bank of India's Economic Research Department has lowered its forecast for the Reserve Bank of India's December rate increase, pointing to easing pressure on the rupee and stronger foreign capital inflows. The change was reported by The Economic Times on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

SBI Research now expects a 25-basis-point increase at the December policy meeting, compared with its earlier 50-basis-point projection. The report said improved external conditions, renewed foreign fund inflows and reduced pressure on the Indian rupee had shifted the balance of probabilities.

The research unit put the chance of the December increase being the final hike in the current cycle at 50:50. It also said the terminal repo rate could reach 5.75 percent. The RBI raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent in October, its first increase in almost four years.

sum: Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the bank's launch of a project to assess and finance new age infrastructure projects, Setty said that globally neither equity or bank deposits are given any special treatment.

"Globally also we have not seen anywhere where the bank deposits are given any special treatment, but at the same time equity instruments are also not given a special treatment in many jurisdictions.In an evolving equity environment, probably those benefits were justified. (But) now I think there should be a level playing field for the financial savings instruments," Setty said.

At present, returns on deposits attract taxation as per a taxpayer's tax slab which may go up to 30% while equity returns are taxed at 12.5% for long-term gains with a holding of more than a year above Rs 1.25 lakh. The Economic Survey released earlier this week also pointed towards the structural change in Indian household savings.
The share of deposits in financial savings having dropped to 35.2% in FY25 from 57.9% in FY12, though higher than the 31.95% reported in FY22.

"Equity investments, which were once ancillary to household balance sheets, have increasingly become a significant component of financial wealth, supported by broader participation and more diversified channels of access," the economic survey said.
